headline: Hasan Mahmud claims historic Test hattrick against Afghanistan
summary: The pacer becomes the first Bangladeshi fast bowler to achieve the feat, leading the Tigers to a 150-run overall lead.
details: Bangladesh dominated the third day of the Test match in Abu Dhabi, bowling out Afghanistan for 240 in their first innings. The visitors claimed six wickets for just 29 runs in a devastating first hour.

Hasan Mahmud entered the history books as the first Bangladeshi pacer to claim a Test hattrick, taking three wickets in three balls. This was only the third hattrick by any Bangladeshi bowler in Tests and the 50th in the history of the format.

Hasan's brilliance was complemented by Ebadot Hossain, who claimed 4-56. Together, they dismantled the Afghan lower order after Ebadot broke a crucial 80-run partnership between Rahmat Shah and Ikram Alikhil.
The pacer finished with a five-wicket haul (5-55), becoming the fastest Bangladeshi pacer to reach 50 Test wickets in just 17 Tests and 29 innings.
Despite the collapse, Afghanistan captain Rahmat Shah stood tall, scoring an unbeaten 105 off 216 deliveries, including 10 fours and two sixes.
Bangladesh began their second innings with a 106-run first-innings lead, but lost two wickets before lunch, reaching 44 for two. They currently hold an overall lead of 150 runs.

headline: 12 killed, 300 injured in Houthi attack on Riyadh airport
summary: Two Bangladeshis are among the dead; the government will repatriate their bodies at state expense.
details: A deadly attack by the Houthi armed group on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, has left 12 people dead and 309 injured.
Two Bangladeshi citizens were among those killed in the blast. The Bangladesh government has decided to bring their bodies back home at state expense.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid Islam announced this during a briefing on Sunday, adding that four other Bangladeshis are currently being treated in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU).
Bangladesh has strongly condemned the attack and called for an immediate end to the conflict and the protection of civilian lives.
The Bangladesh mission in Riyadh is coordinating with Saudi authorities to gather detailed information on the victims and provide necessary assistance to the affected.
The government has urged all Bangladeshis residing in Saudi Arabia to remain safe and is monitoring the security situation at other Saudi airports.
Due to the airport closure and security concerns, multiple flights between Dhaka and Riyadh have been cancelled.
caption:
12 dead and over 300 injured after a Houthi attack on Riyadh airport. Two Bangladeshis were among the victims.

A deadly attack by the Houthi armed group on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, has left 12 people dead and 309 injured.

Two Bangladeshi citizens were among those killed in the blast. The Bangladesh government has decided to bring their bodies back home at state expense.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid Islam announced this during a briefing on Sunday, adding that four other Bangladeshis are currently being treated in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU).

Bangladesh has strongly condemned the attack and called for an immediate end to the conflict and the protection of civilian lives.

The Bangladesh mission in Riyadh is coordinating with Saudi authorities to gather detailed information on the victims and provide necessary assistance to the affected.

The government has urged all Bangladeshis residing in Saudi Arabia to remain safe and is monitoring the security situation at other Saudi airports.

Due to the airport closure and security concerns, multiple flights between Dhaka and Riyadh have been cancelled.
